title: Neguntatogue (Lindenhurst)
summary: Neguntatogue is associated with a neck of land south of Breslau, now Lindenhurst, between Little Neck and Santapogue.
map_geometry_source: approximate modern Neguntatogue Creek / Lindenhurst marker; not exact historical neck or meadow boundary
history_content: Neguntatogue belongs to the south-shore neck and meadow landscape of Babylon town. Nearby names such as Little Neck, Santapogue, Gueguis, and Guscomquorom help place it within a dense cluster of related shore placenames.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Naqueetatogue, Nagunfatogue, Neguntatogue, Neguntetake, Nagunttatauge, Neguntataug, Nagunttatoug, and Naguntatogue. The name is interpreted as abandoned or forsaken land, connecting it with fields left behind after use.

Why Place Names Matter

“Traditional place names provide information about First Peoples and their relationship with the land. Traditional knowledge is often embedded in place names.”

— First Nations Education Steering Committee and First Nations Schools Association, Secondary Science First Peoples (2019), Part One: Foundations, Place Names section
whereintheworld_content: The map placement is an approximate general point near modern Neguntatogue Creek in Lindenhurst, not an exact boundary for the older neck, meadow lot, or creek landscape.
